steps.name: QC and DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: sample_01's ~4x-below-median library size can inflate its dispersion contribution; do not drop it purely on depth without checking whether it is also a compositional/clustering outlier
12000 genes is a pre-filtered/gene-level count file already, so an additional low-count filter should be mild (e.g. require nonzero counts in enough samples) — do not over-filter a set this small
steps.question: After confirming sample_01's low library size does not distort normalization or clustering, what are the DESeq2-moderated log2 fold changes and Wald statistics for treated (cytokine-stimulated) vs control (vehicle) bronchial epithelial samples (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch)?
acceptance_criteria: Raw counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv are loaded and matched on sample ID
Library size / PCA / sample-correlation diagnostics are computed and sample_01 is explicitly flagged and its impact on the treated/control clustering reported

A decision is made and justified on whether sample_01 is retained (relying on DESeq2 size-factor normalization) or excluded as an outlier, based on whether it clusters with its condition group after normalization

DESeq2 is run with design ~condition (treated vs control), producing a full results table (log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) for all genes, with independent filtering and (if the outlier is kept) documented
Shrunk log2FoldChange (apeglm or ashr) is also computed and saved alongside the raw Wald statistic, since the downstream footprint step needs the moderated statistic, not raw counts
Output table is saved with gene symbols as row identifiers matching the counts.csv gene column

steps.name: Footprint-based pathway activity via PROGENy (decoupler mlm)
caveats: The staged PROGENy weight table is an .rda R object (model_human_full: gene, weight, p.value, pathway) — load via rpy2 or an R subprocess and rename columns to source/target/weight before passing to decoupler

PROGENy pathways are historically curated for cancer signaling; several (e.g. Androgen, Estrogen) may be biologically irrelevant to airway epithelium — report but do not overinterpret near-zero activity on those as informative
steps.question: Using the DESeq2 Wald statistics from the treated-vs-control contrast as the footprint signature, which of the 14 PROGENy signaling pathways (e.g. EGFR, MAPK, PI3K, TNFa, NFkB, JAK-STAT, TGFb, Hypoxia, p53, TNFa) show significant directional activity change in cytokine-stimulated versus vehicle bronchial epithelial cells?
acceptance_criteria: The human PROGENy pathway-responsive-gene weight model is loaded from the environment's staged PROGENy human reference and converted to a source/target/weight decoupler-style network (renaming pathway/gene/weight columns)
A single-column (or per-sample) input matrix of the DESeq2 Wald statistic (genes x 1) is built with gene symbols matching the PROGENy network's gene identifiers

decoupler dc.mt.mlm (or an equivalent decoupler multivariate linear model call) is run on this contrast vector against the PROGENy network with an appropriate tmin, producing one activity score and p-value per pathway for the treated-vs-control contrast
Report ranks pathways by absolute activity score with p-values, explicitly stating this is a footprint (perturbation-response-gene) based score, not pathway-member expression
If the PROGENy reference cannot be loaded or converted, this is reported as a hard gap for this step rather than silently substituted with an expression-based proxy

steps.name: TF-activity footprint via CollecTRI/DoRothEA regulons (decoupler ulm)
caveats: CollecTRI is CSV and directly decoupler-ready; DoRothEA is an .rda needing rpy2/R load plus confidence filtering (levels A-C) and column renaming — prefer CollecTRI as primary given it needs no conversion, use DoRothEA as a secondary comparison only if time/resources allow

TF activity inference assumes the regulon (literature-curated, largely non-tissue-specific) applies to bronchial epithelium; a hit means the target-gene footprint is consistent with that TF's activity change, not proof of direct TF engagement in this tissue
steps.question: Which transcription-factor regulons (e.g. NFKB1/RELA, STAT1/STAT3, IRF1, AP-1 family) show significant inferred activity change between cytokine-treated and control bronchial epithelial samples, based on the expression footprint of their target genes rather than the TFs' own expression?
acceptance_criteria: The CollecTRI human regulatory network CSV (source/target/weight) is loaded directly, or DoRothEA human regulons (confidence A-C) are loaded from the staged .rda and converted to source/target/weight
The same DESeq2 Wald-statistic contrast vector from T1S1 is used as input
decoupler dc.mt.ulm is run against the regulon network with tmin filtering, producing a ranked, directional TF activity score and p-value per TF for the contrast

Top TFs by absolute activity (both up and down) are reported with their target-gene overlap counts, and cross-referenced qualitatively against the PROGENy pathway result from T2S1 (e.g. an NFkB/STAT signature at the TF level supporting a PROGENy NFkB/JAK-STAT pathway call, or a mismatch flagged as such)
The distinction between this TF-footprint view and simple differential expression of the TF genes themselves is stated explicitly in the output

steps.name: Orthogonal pathway-member enrichment (ORA/GSEA) for comparison
caveats: GO BP sets are a nested hierarchy — if used, collapse parent/child redundancy before reporting a hit count; hallmark and canonical C2:CP sets are the primary recommended collections here for a cleaner comparison

This ORA/GSEA view answers a different question (which pathways have altered member expression) than the footprint methods in T2 — do not merge the two into one 'active pathways' list without flagging which method produced which call
steps.question: Which canonical signaling pathways (WikiPathways, MSigDB hallmark and canonical C2:CP sets) are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control samples, judged by pathway-member expression rather than footprint — reported specifically as the contrasting view the research question distinguishes from footprint activity?
acceptance_criteria: WikiPathways human GMT and MSigDB human hallmark + canonical pathway (BioCarta/KEGG-MEDICUS/PID) GMTs are loaded from the environment's staged references
Genes are ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (or shrunk log2FC) from T1S1 for a preranked GSEA (fgsea), and a padj<0.05 DE gene list is used for a complementary ORA
fgsea and/or clusterProfiler ORA are run against each gene-set collection, producing NES/enrichment scores and adjusted p-values per pathway

The report explicitly labels this output as the pathway-member-expression view and contrasts its top hits against the PROGENy/TF-footprint results from T2S1/T2S2, noting agreements and discrepancies (e.g. a pathway enriched here but not footprint-active, or vice versa) as the direct answer to the research question's framing
Multiple-testing correction is applied within each gene-set collection separately, not pooled across all collections

plan.title: Footprint-based pathway activity: cytokine vs vehicle bronchial epithelium
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question explicitly asks for pathway activity judged by transcriptional footprint, not by expression of pathway members — this rules out naive member-gene GSEA/ORA on hallmark or KEGG sets and calls for footprint-based methods (PROGENy, and TF-activity via CollecTRI/DoRothEA as a complementary regulatory layer, since TF activity is itself inferred from downstream target expression rather than TF expression). The data is a clean 6-vs-6 unpaired bulk RNA-seq contrast (Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples, single batch) with one flagged low-depth sample (sample_01, ~4x below median library size) that must be handled explicitly rather than silently dropped or silently kept. Track 1 does standard count QC and DESeq2 differential expression to produce a moderated per-gene statistic (Wald stat / shrunk log2FC) — this is the substrate the footprint methods consume, not raw counts, so pathway activity reflects the treatment contrast rather than per-sample noise. Track 2 runs decoupler (mlm for the ~14 PROGENy pathways, and ulm on CollecTRI/DoRothEA-A-C regulons for TF activity) on the DE statistic vector, giving a directional, footprint-based read of which signaling pathways are up- or down-active in treated vs control, distinguishing this explicitly from the pathway-member-expression view. Track 3 cross-checks with WikiPathways/MSigDB canonical-pathway ORA on the DE gene list as an orthogonal, non-footprint reference so the two views (footprint activity vs. member enrichment) can be reported side by side and contrasted per the question's framing. The QC step for sample_01 runs first and gates whether it is kept (down-weighted via size-factor normalization, which DESeq2 does natively) or excluded, with the decision made on evidence (PCA/correlation outlier status) rather than assumption.
